title: What If Every Sea Otter Vanished?

scenes.text: What if every sea otter vanished? The kelp forests would be the first to feel it.
Sea otters eat sea urchins. Urchins graze on kelp.
With otters around, urchins hide in cracks and nibble drifting scraps.
Without them, urchins eat living kelp heavily, and a forest can be mown down.
A UC Santa Cruz study of forty years of data found kelp can absorb up to twelve times more carbon dioxide when urchins are kept in check.
Researchers valued that otter-powered carbon removal at roughly two hundred to four hundred million dollars. One small swimmer holding up a whole forest.
